stem: A pregnant client with placenta accreta spectrum is scheduled for delivery at a center equipped to manage major obstetric hemorrhage. Which pre-delivery nursing coordination action is most important?

options.A: Confirm that the blood bank has been notified and that compatibility testing and rapid access to blood products are coordinated according to the facility’s hemorrhage plan.
options.B: Wait until active hemorrhage begins before contacting the blood bank because advance coordination provides no benefit.
options.C: Rely on crystalloid availability alone because placenta accreta spectrum rarely requires large-volume blood transfusion.
options.D: Cancel the client’s hemorrhage risk assessment once blood-bank preparation is complete because compatibility planning replaces other maternal safety planning.

rationale: A is correct. ACOG guidance for placenta accreta spectrum recommends delivery planning at appropriately resourced centers with access to a blood bank capable of massive transfusion and specifically recommends notification and collaboration with the blood bank because large-volume transfusion is frequently needed. Pre-delivery coordination can address compatibility needs and rapid access to blood products as part of the broader hemorrhage plan. B creates avoidable delay, C understates the hemorrhage risk, and D incorrectly treats blood-bank preparation as a substitute for comprehensive risk assessment and team planning.
educational_objective: Coordinate blood-bank readiness before delivery for clients at high risk of major obstetric hemorrhage so compatible blood products can be accessed rapidly as part of a comprehensive hemorrhage plan.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
source_document_title: Placenta Accreta Spectrum — Obstetric Care Consensus
source_locator: Delivery planning — centers managing placenta accreta spectrum should have access to a blood bank capable of employing massive transfusion protocols; notification and collaboration with the blood bank is recommended in concert with delivery and surgical planning because large-volume blood transfusion is frequently required and crossmatching can be difficult
source_claim_supported: For placenta accreta spectrum and other high-risk hemorrhage planning, advance blood-bank collaboration is recommended so compatibility needs and rapid access to blood products are addressed before bleeding occurs.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate high-risk care, anticipate resource needs, and collaborate with interprofessional services before planned procedures
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — blood-bank preparedness for anticipated obstetric hemorrhage
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item because a blanket rule that every high-risk postpartum-hemorrhage client must have a specific pre-delivery type-and-cross protocol was more specific than the accessible source. The final version uses ACOG’s direct recommendation for blood-bank notification/collaboration and rapid transfusion capability in a clearly high-risk placenta accreta scenario. Category corrected from infection control to Management of Care.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: placenta accreta spectrum / hemorrhage preparedness / blood-bank coordination
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against current ACOG placenta accreta spectrum guidance. The need for massive-transfusion-capable blood-bank access and advance notification/collaboration are explicit.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A uses advance coordination and compatibility testing according to facility plan without inventing a universal number of crossmatched units or a specific transfusion ratio. It keeps blood-bank readiness within a broader hemorrhage-preparedness framework.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it implements the direct ACOG blood-bank planning recommendation.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; waiting until active hemorrhage undermines anticipatory planning in a known high-risk case.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; major blood loss and transfusion are recognized risks in placenta accreta spectrum.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; blood-bank preparation complements rather than replaces comprehensive risk assessment and multidisciplinary planning.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A provides the anticipatory interprofessional preparation supported by the source.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address pre-delivery resource planning for the same high-risk client.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is the best fit because the nurse coordinates resources and interprofessional readiness before a high-risk delivery.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked placenta accreta scope, blood-bank collaboration wording, compatibility-testing specificity, avoidance of universal type-and-cross quantities, resource-planning category, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
